Thanks Laura — read through Sara's quote. Initial notes: 

1) Master Services Agreement (MSA) vs SOW: confirm whether the SOW contains new IP transfer language. If so, push it to standard Redwood MSA language.
2) Data residency & audit logs: the quote references log retention of 90 days; we should require 1 year for auditability (or a paid retention add-on).
3) Termination assistance: add a 90-day export / handover clause with post-termination access for existing contracts.
4) Liability cap: push for mutual cap tied to fees over the prior 12 months rather than a flat low cap.
5) Subprocessors: request an up-to-date subprocessors list and an attestation of SOC2 Type II (latest report).

Please share the current Ironclad MSA and any redlines you already have. If we plan to consolidate to DocuSign for e-sign, I need to see an integration/feature parity checklist (e.g., conditional fields, bulk send, automated routing) so we can confirm CLM → e-sign mapping.

Related links: SOC2 portal link and our standard Redwood MSA template: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0A1Example/CLM_Renewals

Quick finance read: thanks for pulling the usage snapshot. High level — we spent ~ $185k on CLM & e-sign in FY25 (Ironclad + DocuSign combined). Ironclad renewal as quoted is +12% ARR on current spend if we keep seat counts flat.

Options and impact (ballpark):
- Renew Ironclad at quoted terms: +12% ARR, predictable, no migration cost.
- Ask for multi-year + volume discount: expect 6–9% off list for a 2-year commit, and additional flexibility on seat pooling.
- Consolidate to DocuSign for all e-sign (migrate templates + API integration): potential ~18% ARR reduction over 12 months but one-time migration & engineering cost ~ $45k and 3–6 weeks of effort.

Budget/constraints: Q2 commitments should be below $250k additional run-rate unless sales expansion covers it. If we can get a two-year lock and a price cap, finance is comfortable recommending commit.

Attachment: Finance_cost_model_2026.xlsx (spreadsheet)
